samples.summary: `canUndo()`/`canRedo()` were not gated with the new `readOnly` refusal, so the store now advertises history it will refuse to replay
samples.evidence: The delta adds `if (this.readOnly) return { success: false };` to `undo()` (yorkie-store.ts:1285) and `redo()` (:1291), but the sibling predicates the `Store` interface exposes for exactly this question are untouched: `canUndo(): boolean { return this.doc.history.canUndo(); }` (packages/frontend/src/app/spreadsheet/yorkie-store.ts:1370-1372) and `canRedo()` (:1374-1376). Consumers of the interface — e.g. the hunt harness reader `"sheet.canUndo": () => requireSheet(state).store.canUndo()` (packages/frontend/src/app/harness/hunt/bridge.ts:427), and any future toolbar affordance that mirrors the notes/slides pattern at packages/frontend/src/app/notes/notes-toolbar.tsx:417 — will read `true` on a read-only mount while `undo()` now returns `{ success: false }`. Nothing is visibly broken today (the sheets toolbar does not consult `canUndo`), but the two halves of the same contract now disagree. Fix belongs on the new code: add the same `this.readOnly` short-circuit to `canUndo`/`canRedo`.

samples.summary: The task doc's Review section records the exact opposite of what this delta implements ("the acknowledgement round-trip was not needed")
samples.evidence: docs/tasks/active/20260917-sheets-undo-selection-todo.md:169-175 states: "A pending `undoJumpTarget` survived a revision restore. ... Cleared in `handleHistoryRestored` ... The suggested acknowledgement round-trip was not needed: the restore is the only remount, and it is exactly where the target stops meaning anything." This delta adds precisely that acknowledgement round-trip (`onUndoJumpHandled`) on the grounds that the restore is NOT the only remount. The doc now records a rejected design as the landed one, and the "App" row at :127 lists only ``sheet-view.tsx` `undoJumpTarget` / `onUndoJump` props, `document-detail.tsx` `handleUndoJump`` — it does not mention `onUndoJumpHandled` or the new `shared-document.tsx` host.

samples.summary: Design doc still names `DocumentLayout` as the only host that follows a cross-tab undo, and does not record the new store-level read-only refusal
samples.evidence: docs/design/sheets/sheet.md:585-590 says `Sheet` "reports it through `setOnUndoTabJump` ... and `DocumentLayout` switches tabs and hands the selection to the new mount via `undoJumpTarget`". As of this delta a second host does the same — `SharedDocumentLayout` (packages/frontend/src/app/shared/shared-document.tsx:221-234, 327-334) — and the selection hand-off now includes a handled-acknowledgement (`onUndoJumpHandled`) plus a `readOnly` refusal inside `YorkieStore.undo/redo`. None of that appears in the design doc. Nested design docs are not link-checked by CI, so nothing else will flag this.

samples.summary: The handled-acknowledgement only fires from a mounted `SheetView`, so a target that unmounts before it is applied still survives to be applied later
samples.evidence: `onUndoJumpHandled` is fired only after `sheet.focusUndoSelection(...)` succeeds (packages/frontend/src/app/spreadsheet/sheet-view.tsx:1463-1471); the effect returns early while the engine is still initialising (`if (!sheet) return;` at :1464). If the user switches to a datasource or lakehouse tab in that window, `SheetView` is replaced by the `DataSourceView`/`LakehouseView` branch (packages/frontend/src/app/documents/document-detail.tsx:757-766; mirrored at packages/frontend/src/app/shared/shared-document.tsx:322-325) and its mount-local `lastHandledUndoJumpRequestIdRef` is discarded while the host's `undoJumpTarget` is still set. Returning to the original sheet tab remounts `SheetView` and the stale target is applied, yanking the selection from an undo long past — the very failure the new callback's doc comment claims to close. A host-side clear (e.g. dropping the target whenever `activeTab` is not a sheet, or expiring it on tab change) would close the remaining hole.

finding.summary: Shared-document sheet view is editable for the `editor` share role but never passes `onUndoJump`/`undoJumpTarget`, so cross-tab undo stays silently broken there — and the new prop doc asserts the opposite
finding.evidence: `packages/frontend/src/app/shared/shared-document.tsx:300` renders `<SheetView tabId={activeTabId} readOnly={readOnly} peerJumpTarget={peerJumpTarget} />` with `readOnly = resolved.role === "viewer"` (line 198), i.e. an `editor`-role share link gets a fully writable engine with Cmd+Z enabled. That layout has its own multi-tab state (`activeTabId`, line 200) and already implements the identical two-step jump for peers (lines 228-237), but no `onUndoJump`/`undoJumpTarget` wiring. With `onUndoJump` omitted, `Sheet.applyUndoSelection` returns early for `otherTab` selections, so an undo of a step in another tab mutates the CRDT and appears to do nothing — exactly the defect this PR fixes for `document-detail.tsx`. The new JSDoc at `packages/frontend/src/app/spreadsheet/sheet-view.tsx:163-167` claims the omission is "the read-only share view … moot there since undo is disabled", which is false for the editor role. Fix belongs in shared-document.tsx (mirror the peer-jump wiring) or, at minimum, correct the comment.

verdict.reason: The absence claim is false at the exact location cited. `SharedDocumentLayout` in packages/frontend/src/app/shared/shared-document.tsx declares `undoJumpTarget` state and an `undoJumpSeq` ref (lines 208-212), defines `handleUndoJump` (lines 221-225, which sets `activeTabId` to `selection.tabId` then publishes `{selection, requestId}`) and `handleUndoJumpHandled` (lines 227-229), and passes all three props to the grid: `<SheetView tabId={activeTabId} readOnly={readOnly} peerJumpTarget={peerJumpTarget} undoJumpTarget={undoJumpTarget} onUndoJump={handleUndoJump} onUndoJumpHandled={handleUndoJumpHandled} />` (lines 327-334). The file also imports `UndoSelection` (line 16) and declares an `UndoJumpTarget` type (lines 88-91), and its own JSDoc (lines 214-220) explicitly addresses the editor-role case the reviewer says is unhandled. The reviewer's quoted render line and line numbers do not match the file. The secondary claim about the JSDoc is likewise inaccurate: sheet-view.tsx:163-168 says the omission is acceptable only for a `viewer` share link, and shared-document.tsx passes the callbacks unconditionally regardless of `readOnly`, so the comment is consistent with the code. No bypassing or unwired site exists for this contract in the shared path.
